title: A Gravity for the Terminal Again
premise: Jonah Iversen, a xenolinguist who decoded the alien 'Chorus' language and then fled its influence, discovers his own name on the manifest of the Meridian, a ship destroyed three years ago — evidence someone is resurrecting his erased past to frame him as a traitor. Hunted by both the Earth Directorate and Chorus sympathizers, he traces the forged manifest to Director Sela Kwan, who plans to broadcast a fabricated Chorus ultimatum and seize emergency power over the colonies. Jonah must deliver the real message — a genuine Chorus transmission he's carried unknowingly in his own altered dreams — before Earth's last transmission loop closes in nine days. In the end, he broadcasts the truth at the cost of his ability to ever speak human language again, ending the war by becoming, permanently, a bridge between species.
about_author: Freya Vane is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to voices crossing oceans that never met. She writes science fiction about people caught between languages, loyalties, and tides.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Jonah hauls ore through contested orbits, keeping his head down and his dreams medicated. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: weary routine masking grief for the linguist he used to be.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: A customs clerk shows Jonah a cargo manifest listing him aboard the Meridian — destroyed with all hands three years ago. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: cold dread; his invisibility has been punctured.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: Jonah investigates the forgery, finding the Meridian's black box was recovered but sealed by Directorate order. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: stubborn curiosity overriding survival instinct.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Chorus
chapters.summary: Off his medication, Jonah dreams in the alien language again — and realizes the dreams contain structured content, not noise. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: terror mixed with homesickness for a language not his own.

chapters.title: Kwan's Quiet Office
chapters.summary: Director Sela Kwan offers Jonah protection if he testifies that Chorus sympathizers forged the manifest. He recognizes her voice from the Meridian's final transmission. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: the trap closing gently, almost kindly.

chapters.title: Runners in the Dark
chapters.summary: Sympathizer pilot Amara Osei extracts Jonah from the station before Directorate agents can detain him. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people who trust no one.

chapters.title: What the Black Box Keeps
chapters.summary: Amara reveals sympathizers hold a copy of the black box; its audio proves Kwan ordered the Meridian scuttled. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Nine Days of Silence
chapters.summary: They learn Earth's last open transmission loop closes in nine days; after that, only Kwan's network can broadcast system-wide. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: the clock becomes a character, pressing on every scene.

chapters.title: The Translator's Wound
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how decoding the Chorus rewired Jonah's language centers, why he fled, what he abandoned. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: self-forgiveness beginning, painfully.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Halcyon
chapters.summary: A Directorate checkpoint nearly catches them; Jonah talks them through using Chorus cadence patterns to spoof clearance codes. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: first taste of his gift as power rather than curse.

chapters.title: Kwan Ascendant
chapters.summary: Kwan stages a false Chorus attack on a colony relay, cementing public fear and her emergency authority. POV: Kwan. Emotional beat: chilling competence; corruption dressed as duty.

chapters.title: The Message in the Marrow
chapters.summary: Jonah decodes his recurring dream fully: it is a genuine Chorus transmission — an offer of coexistence — lodged in his memory like shrapnel. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: awe and horror; he is the message.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Refinery
chapters.summary: A sympathizer cell sells their location; Amara is captured covering Jonah's escape. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: Kwan interrogates Amara, offering her everything to denounce Jonah; Amara stalls, learning Kwan's broadcast schedule. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: defiance under pressure, quiet heroism.

chapters.title: The Loop's Last Throat
chapters.summary: Jonah infiltrates the transmission hub disguised as maintenance crew, mapping the loop's architecture. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension, small victories.

chapters.title: What Power Promises
chapters.summary: Kwan privately rehearses her fabricated ultimatum; a subordinate objects and is quietly disappeared. POV: Kwan. Emotional beat: the moment she stops believing she is lying.

chapters.title: Two Voices, One Channel
chapters.summary: Jonah breaks Amara out during transfer; they race to the hub as the loop begins its final cycle. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: desperate partnership, love unspoken but certain.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax: Jonah seizes the transmitter and speaks the true Chorus message live, while Kwan broadcasts her forgery simultaneously — two truths colliding across every speaker in the system. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: transcendent terror; he gives up human speech mid-broadcast.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Voice
chapters.summary: The Chorus respond to the authentic signal, standing down; Kwan's fraud unravels as recordings surface. She is arrested, still insisting she saved everyone. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: vindication without triumph.

chapters.title: The Man Who Speaks Tides
chapters.summary: Jonah, unable to form fluent human sentences, communicates through writing, gesture, and Chorus song; colonists begin learning from him. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: loss transfigured into belonging.

chapters.title: Gravity for the Terminal Again
chapters.summary: Months later, the first human-Chorus joint crew launches; Jonah serves as living translator. Amara stays beside him. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity remade rather than restored.

chapters.title: Last Transmission Loop
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Jonah records a message for future generations in both languages, knowing it will outlive him. The loop opens once more, and this time nothing false travels through it. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: quiet hope; the war ended by a voice that gave itself away.
